strengths: The paper proposes a clear and useful change to the 3DGS pipeline: replacing iterative densification with dense correspondence-based triangulated initialization. This is conceptually simple but addresses an important bottleneck in 3DGS optimization.

The empirical results are strong on standard novel-view synthesis benchmarks. On Mip-NeRF360, Tanks & Temples, and Deep Blending, the method improves LPIPS/SSIM over several quality-focused 3DGS variants while using fewer Gaussians than standard 3DGS in the 30K-step setting.

The paper evaluates both quality and efficiency, and explicitly includes initialization time for the proposed method. The early-stop results show that the initialization can provide useful quality after 5K steps, supporting the central claim of faster convergence.

Ablations are relevant: the paper studies densification versus no densification, different dense matching backbones, depth-based initialization, noise robustness, Gaussian motion during optimization, and sensitivity to the number of reference views/matches.

The method is potentially practical because it modifies initialization rather than requiring a new renderer or optimizer, and the demonstrated combination with Taming-3DGS supports some degree of compatibility with acceleration techniques.
weaknesses: The technical description of triangulation and initialization is not fully rigorous. The projection matrix dimensions and equations are confusing, and Eq. 6 sets the right-hand side to zero despite the usual inhomogeneous constants from the projection matrix. This makes the method harder to verify and raises concerns about whether the manuscript accurately specifies the implemented algorithm.

Several important implementation details needed for reproducibility are missing or underspecified, including correspondence confidence thresholds, sampling strategy, outlier filtering, duplicate handling, exact scale initialization formula, nearest-neighbor selection details, and the computational configuration of the dense matcher.

The approach depends on a pretrained dense matching model and sufficient multi-view overlap. The paper does not deeply analyze failure cases such as textureless regions, repetitive patterns, specular/transparent surfaces, inaccurate camera poses, sparse or wide-baseline captures, and scenes where dense matching is unreliable.

The originality is moderate rather than high: using dense correspondences and triangulation for better 3D initialization is a natural extension of multi-view geometry. The value is mainly in demonstrating that this initialization can replace 3DGS densification effectively, not in a fundamentally new algorithmic mechanism.

Some claims are broader than the evidence. Compatibility with other acceleration techniques is asserted generally but experimentally shown mainly with Taming-3DGS. Sparse/front-facing robustness is mentioned only through a public demo rather than a systematic benchmark.

The evaluation is solid but still limited to the common 13-scene protocol. Broader testing on larger scenes, more diverse captures, and explicit wall-clock breakdowns for matching versus optimization would be important for assessing practical deployment.

Presentation has multiple notation and writing issues, including inconsistent dimensions, imprecise terminology, and grammatical problems. These are mostly fixable, but the mathematical ambiguities are material because they affect reproducibility.

strengths: The paper addresses a real bottleneck in 3D Gaussian Splatting: slow convergence induced by incremental densification. The idea of replacing part of this process with dense correspondence-based initialization is simple, relevant, and potentially useful.

The experimental section covers the standard Mip-NeRF360, Tanks & Temples, and Deep Blending benchmarks, and compares against several meaningful 3DGS variants and acceleration baselines. The reported LPIPS/SSIM gains, especially on Tanks & Temples and Deep Blending, suggest that the initialization can improve perceptual quality.

The method is plausibly orthogonal to rasterizer/optimizer improvements, and the combination with Taming 3DGS is a useful demonstration that initialization quality can complement existing acceleration methods.
The ablations on matching backbones, densification, number of references/matches, and noise sensitivity are helpful and support the high-level claim that geometry-aware initialization matters.
weaknesses: The technical formulation is not sufficiently rigorous. The triangulation derivation contains apparent dimensional and mathematical inconsistencies: projection matrices are described as 4x3 rather than the usual 3x4, the notation transposes homogeneous coordinates in a confusing way, and the least-squares system is written with b=0 while solving directly for a 3D point, which would be ill-posed unless the homogeneous scale/fixed coordinate terms are handled properly. Cheirality, degeneracies, outlier rejection, duplicate correspondences, and confidence filtering are also not specified in enough detail.

The central novelty is relatively incremental. Dense matching plus triangulation is a classical multi-view reconstruction pipeline, and the paper mostly repurposes this as a 3DGS initialization. The submission would be stronger if it clarified what is technically new beyond using a modern pretrained matcher to seed Gaussians densely.

The evidence does not fully support some of the strongest claims. On Mip-NeRF360, the proposed method is not uniformly superior across metrics: 3DGS-MCMC has higher PSNR than Ours+3DGS, and the gains over several strong baselines are often modest. The statement that the method outperforms both quality-focused and speed-optimized methods is therefore overstated.

Runtime comparisons are hard to interpret. The method relies on a pretrained dense matching network and a large initialization pipeline, but the exact matching resolution, batching, number of image pairs, hardware utilization, and preprocessing details are not sufficiently reported. Some baselines use paper-reported numbers or different GPUs, while others are retrained, which weakens the fairness of the timing claims.

The 5K-step efficiency setting uses substantially more Gaussians than several efficient baselines, e.g. MiniSplatting and EAGLES, so the claim of efficiency is mixed: wall-clock time improves in some cases, but model size and rendering/storage implications are less favorable.

The reproducibility details are incomplete. Important choices such as correspondence thresholding, sampling distribution, duplicate merging, scale initialization constants, handling of failed matches, neighbor selection beyond a high-level Frobenius-distance description, and exact pretrained matcher configuration are either missing or scattered. Without code, reproducing the reported initialization would be difficult.

Several evaluations that would test the method's actual limitations are missing. Since the approach depends on reliable dense correspondences, the paper should evaluate low-overlap views, repetitive/textureless scenes, reflective or non-Lambertian surfaces, dynamic content, inaccurate camera poses, and memory/runtime scaling with image count. The paper mentions reflective surfaces as a weakness but does not analyze it experimentally.

Presentation quality is uneven. The writing repeatedly overclaims, contains grammar/notation issues, and some figures/tables are difficult to read. These are not merely cosmetic because they obscure key implementation and technical details needed to assess correctness.

strengths: The paper presents a clear and useful idea: replace iterative 3DGS densification with dense initialization from triangulated 2D correspondences. This targets a real bottleneck in 3DGS training and is orthogonal to many optimizer/rasterizer accelerations.

Empirical results are strong on standard dense-view novel-view-synthesis benchmarks. On Mip-NeRF360, Tanks&Temples, and Deep Blending, the proposed initialization improves LPIPS/SSIM over 3DGS and several quality-oriented variants, and the 5K-step variants are competitive with speed-focused baselines while using substantially fewer optimization steps.

The ablations support the main mechanism. The paper studies densification on/off, alternative matchers, depth-based initialization, hyperparameter sensitivity, noise robustness, and Gaussian motion/path length, which collectively make the convergence argument more convincing than a table-only comparison.
The method is practical and modular: it builds on the original 3DGS optimization after initialization, can be combined with Taming-3DGS, and does not require changing the core rendering formulation.
The paper is generally well motivated and understandable, with helpful qualitative comparisons and supplementary visualizations explaining coverage, matching confidence, and initialization noise.
weaknesses: The fairness and completeness of comparisons are somewhat uneven. Some baseline numbers are taken from papers or rely on assumptions about Gaussian counts, while others are rerun on A100. The table also reports only training time for most non-initialization baselines, whereas the proposed method includes matching/initialization time; however, the preprocessing assumptions for COLMAP/SfM and other baselines are not fully standardized or dissected.

Reproducibility is not yet fully convincing. Important implementation details are underspecified, including exact match confidence thresholds, sampling strategy, duplicate/outlier filtering after triangulation, scale initialization formula, camera-neighbor selection details, and complete hyperparameter settings. No code-release statement is apparent.

The method depends on pretrained dense matchers, accurate camera poses, and sufficient cross-view overlap. The paper acknowledges undercovered regions and reflective-surface issues, but does not provide a systematic failure analysis or quantify performance under poor matches, sparse views, inaccurate poses, dynamic content, or strong non-Lambertian effects.

The claimed superiority over quality-focused methods is supported mainly by averages; the appendix per-scene tables appear to report only the proposed variants, making it harder to inspect whether gains are consistent across scenes and metrics relative to all baselines.

Some technical presentation details are sloppy and could confuse reproduction: the projection-matrix dimensions/equations are written inconsistently, notation is occasionally imprecise, and there are typos such as “absoulte” and “ptimisation.” These are mostly presentation issues, but the triangulation derivation should be cleaned up.

The contribution is conceptually natural given known multi-view triangulation and dense matching, so the originality lies more in applying this initialization effectively to eliminate 3DGS densification than in a new geometric formulation. This is still useful, but not a fundamental algorithmic breakthrough.

strengths: Clear and useful idea: replacing iterative 3DGS densification with dense correspondence-based triangulated initialization is a practical contribution, and the paper explains why this can shorten optimization trajectories.

Empirical results are strong on standard novel-view synthesis benchmarks. EDGS improves LPIPS substantially over 3DGS and competitive 3DGS variants on Mip-NeRF360, Tanks&Temples, and Deep Blending, while using fewer final Gaussians and disabling densification.

The evaluation includes relevant ablations: matcher choice, correspondence/reprojection sampling terms, spherical harmonics initialization, hyperparameter sensitivity, noise robustness, alternative depth/COLMAP/random initializations, and plug-in use with existing adaptive density-control methods.

The paper is unusually careful about reporting initialization time for EDGS, and the supplementary material gives useful implementation details such as reference-view count, nearest-neighbor count, sample count, thresholds, RoMa runtime, and memory use.
The contribution is modular: the initialization improves plain 3DGS and also improves AbsGS, 3DGS-MCMC, and Taming 3DGS without increasing reported Gaussian count or total time.
weaknesses: The method description has technical inconsistencies that hurt confidence and reproducibility. The projection matrix dimensions are inconsistent across the paper, the triangulation derivation appears to set up a homogeneous least-squares problem with a zero right-hand side/trivial solution unless interpreted as standard DLT, and Eq. 11/sampling notation is imprecise about how probabilities are normalized and aggregated.

The role and cost of the external dense matcher are not fully analyzed. EDGS depends on RoMa or similar pretrained dense matching, with about 120 seconds and 15GB GPU memory for initialization; this is acceptable but changes the dependency profile relative to vanilla 3DGS, and robustness to matcher domain shift, low-texture scenes, exposure changes, rolling shutter, or poor camera calibration is not deeply evaluated.

Some fairness issues remain in the runtime comparisons. EDGS includes its initialization time, but baselines generally count only optimization time, while all methods may have different preprocessing assumptions; some baseline numbers are re-run, some are taken from papers, and hardware differs for several entries.

The main benchmark breadth is moderate: the core evidence is concentrated on the standard 9+2+2 scene suite, with sparse/front-facing/synthetic results mostly in the supplement and not as comprehensive. There is little analysis of failure cases or scenes where dense correspondences are unreliable.

Several claims are stronger than the evidence warrants. The paper says the sampling captures semantic confidence and that selected correspondences remain consistent across multiple views, but the actual procedure mainly thresholds matcher confidence and reprojection error over pairwise neighbors. The claimed elimination of densification is convincing for tested settings, but not established as broadly true across more challenging capture regimes.

Clarity is generally good, but presentation has minor issues: table captions occasionally overstate wins across all metrics, some notation is overloaded, and important implementation choices such as pruning, scale initialization, and exact neighbor selection deserve more precise main-paper treatment.

strengths: The paper addresses an important practical bottleneck in 3D Gaussian Splatting: slow convergence and dependence on iterative densification. Replacing densification with dense correspondence-based initialization is a clear, useful direction.

The experimental evidence is reasonably broad for novel view synthesis: Mip-NeRF360, Tanks & Temples, and Deep Blending are evaluated, with standard PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS metrics plus runtime and Gaussian count.

The main quantitative results are promising, especially LPIPS. EDGS improves over the authors' retrained 3DGS baseline on Mip-NeRF360 from 0.215 to 0.141 LPIPS, and also improves LPIPS on Tanks & Temples and Deep Blending.

The paper includes relevant ablations: matching backbone choice, sampling components, spherical harmonics initialization, noise robustness, sparse-view behavior, and comparisons to depth/COLMAP/random initializations.
The method appears practically compatible with other 3DGS variants. Table 3 suggests EDGS initialization improves AbsGS, 3DGS-MCMC, and Taming 3DGS without increasing final Gaussian count or runtime.
weaknesses: The novelty is incremental rather than fundamental. The method combines dense learned matching, triangulation, filtering, and 3DGS initialization; these are sensible engineering choices, but the conceptual leap beyond 'initialize 3DGS from dense correspondences' is limited.

Several claims are overstated. The paper says EDGS is faster and improves reconstruction quality across all benchmarks, but the 30K EDGS runtime is comparable to or slower than retrained 3DGS on Mip-NeRF360 and Deep Blending, and it is not uniformly best on PSNR/SSIM. The strongest case is perceptual quality, not uniformly better quality and speed.

The comparison is not fully clean. EDGS relies on RoMa, a large pretrained dense matcher, while baselines do not receive an equivalent learned correspondence prior. The paper reports EDGS initialization time, but the dependence on the pretrained model, its training data, and possible domain overlap are not analyzed.

The method section has technical imprecision. Projection matrix dimensions and notation appear inconsistent, the triangulation equation is written with a zero vector b in a way that obscures the actual linear system, and the sampling distribution is described as products of uniform distributions over thresholded sets, which is not mathematically clear enough to reproduce exactly.

Reproducibility is only moderate. Important implementation details are in the appendix, but the paper does not provide code, exact baseline configurations, random seed sensitivity, or enough detail on camera-neighbor selection, pruning behavior, and scale initialization to make faithful reproduction straightforward.

The evaluation does not fully isolate where gains come from. EDGS is compared to denser COLMAP and depth initialization, but there is no equally strong baseline using dense matcher triangulation with simpler filtering, multi-view stereo/depth fusion, or direct RoMa-derived point clouds under matched Gaussian counts.

The sparse-view claims are weak. In the appendix, EDGS is competitive but not consistently better than SparseGS; for example, it has lower PSNR in both 12-view and 24-view settings. This should be framed as applicability rather than evidence that densification is broadly unnecessary.

The paper under-discusses failure modes. Dense correspondence methods can fail under specular surfaces, repetitive textures, non-Lambertian regions, motion, low overlap, or inaccurate poses, but the robustness analysis only adds synthetic noise to initialized colors/coordinates rather than testing realistic matcher failures.

Presentation quality is uneven. Some tables have formatting issues, captions contain overclaims, and several qualitative claims rely on cropped examples without enough systematic analysis of artifacts such as floaters, geometry accuracy, or extreme-view consistency.

strengths: The paper proposes a clear and useful idea: replacing iterative 3DGS densification with a dense initialization obtained by triangulating dense 2D correspondences. This is well motivated by the slow optimization path of standard densification and is a natural fit for improving convergence.

The empirical results are strong overall. EDGS improves LPIPS substantially over standard 3DGS and several recent 3DGS variants on Mip-NeRF360, Tanks&Temples, and Deep Blending, while using fewer Gaussians and disabling densification. The early-stopping results are also compelling, showing good quality at 5K/10K steps.

The method is shown to be complementary to adaptive density-control methods. Adding EDGS initialization to AbsGS, 3DGS-MCMC, and Taming 3DGS improves reported metrics without increasing final Gaussian count or training time, which supports the claim that the initialization itself is broadly useful.

The ablations are meaningful: the paper studies different dense matchers, confidence/reprojection sampling terms, spherical harmonics initialization, noise robustness, number of reference views/correspondences/neighbors, alternative initializations, and sparse-view settings. These analyses make the main claims more convincing.

The paper is mostly clear and reproducible at the algorithmic level. The supplement provides important implementation details such as the RoMa matcher, 180 reference views, 2 nearest neighbors, 20K correspondences per reference view, thresholds, initialization runtime, memory, and optimization protocol.
weaknesses: The novelty is solid but somewhat incremental conceptually: the work combines known ingredients, dense feature matching, triangulation, and 3DGS initialization. The main contribution is the effective engineering and validation of this combination rather than a fundamentally new reconstruction formulation.

The technical description of triangulation and notation has issues. Projection matrices are inconsistently described, and the linear system in Sec. 3.3 is confusingly written with a zero vector b and homogeneous coordinates, which could imply a trivial solution if interpreted literally. This is likely a presentation problem, but it matters for reproducibility.

The runtime and efficiency story is not uniformly favorable. Full EDGS training on Mip-NeRF360 is reported as 27 minutes including initialization, comparable to or slower than retrained 3DGS at 26 minutes and slower than several efficient methods. The strongest efficiency claim comes from early stopping, where quality is good but not uniformly best across all metrics.

The headline quality claims should be qualified. EDGS has excellent LPIPS, but on Mip-NeRF360 full 3DGS-MCMC reports higher SSIM and PSNR, and on Deep Blending ScaffoldGS reports better PSNR/SSIM. The paper sometimes states state-of-the-art or improved quality broadly when the advantage is strongest in perceptual quality rather than all metrics.

The method relies on a pretrained dense correspondence model and reasonably accurate camera poses. Failure cases for poor matching, large textureless regions, dynamic objects, specular/repetitive structures, or inaccurate poses are not deeply explored. This dependency also complicates the interpretation of EDGS as a purely 3DGS-side improvement.

Some comparisons are not perfectly clean: a few baseline numbers are taken from papers or different GPUs, and the inclusion/exclusion of initialization/preprocessing costs varies across methods. The authors do report EDGS initialization time, which is good, but the comparison would be stronger with uniformly measured wall-clock pipelines for all baselines.

Reproducibility would benefit from more precise details on sampling aggregation, scale initialization, pruning settings, and how invalid or inconsistent correspondences are handled. The current description is adequate for understanding but may leave implementation ambiguity.
